source.title: A hidden Markov model to detect regime changes in cryptoasset markets

exact_source_method.objective: Explain and predict Bitcoin price dynamics across exchange markets through latent regime states.
exact_source_method.observed_vector: Y_t is the vector of Bitcoin USD market prices across the included exchanges at time t.
exact_source_method.next_state_prediction: Compute conditional P(Z_{t+1}|Y_{1:T}) under the fitted model and choose the state with the highest conditional probability.
exact_source_method.price_forecast: Associate the predicted state with the mean exchange prices under that state.

source_to_registry_mismatch.conclusion: The current RIE-CAND-0028 YATL hypothesis is an internal adaptation, not a direct reproduction of the published method.

unresolved_yatl_adaptation_choices: Choose source-faithful versus YATL-native observation features; no return/volatility feature set is justified by this source alone.
Choose BTC-only, BTC/ETH joint, or multi-venue architecture.
Freeze timeframe; source evidence is daily and intraday is only proposed as future work.
Freeze training window and refit/update schedule.
Freeze deterministic initialization, convergence, and failed-fit behavior.
Freeze state-label canonicalization using training-only information; HMM state labels are exchangeable.
Freeze probability-to-eligibility/exposure mapping, including UNKNOWN state semantics.
Freeze whether state count is fixed at three or searched; any search must consume an explicit bounded trial budget.
Add conditional-edge detector metrics: false activation/deactivation, recognition lag, missed opportunity, loss before shutdown, re-entry lag, false re-entry.
Define base/stress cost mapping and opportunity-preservation gates.
blind_spot_findings: Using the published three-state result as if it were universally optimal would transfer an in-sample source selection into a different market/timeframe.
Mapping latent states to bear/stable/bull after viewing their realized periods can leak future information unless YATL canonicalizes labels from training-only statistics.
HMM complexity introduces initialization/local-optimum and model-selection degrees of freedom that must be preregistered.
The paper models nonstationary price levels with Gaussian state emissions; direct reuse on intraday crypto should not be assumed valid.
Source prediction quality is price-RMSE evidence, not trading-edge evidence.
